title: Pilgrim's Progress
episode: Episode 6 — The Knight, the Cage and the Dream

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: Christian had already seen three rooms in the House of the Interpreter. But the old owl had more to show him.

beats.speaker: Interpreter
beats.text: This next room is a picture of courage. Watch closely, Christian.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: Before a splendid palace stood a crowd of people. They longed to go in, but none of them dared. For the doorway was guarded by armed men.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Why do they only stand there? The door is wide open!

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: Then one brave man stepped up to the table, where a man sat with a book and a pen.

beats.speaker: Knight
beats.text: Write down my name, sir! I am going in!

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: He put on his helmet, drew his sword, and charged at the guards. He took many hard blows... but he would not turn back.
beats.say: He put on his helmet, drew his sword, and charged at the guards! He took many hard blows... but he would not turn back.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: And from inside the palace, a joyful song rang out: Come in, come in! Eternal glory you shall win!
beats.say: And from inside the palace, a joyful song rang out. Come in, come in! Eternal glory you shall win!

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Oh! I think I know what this one means!

beats.speaker: Interpreter
beats.text: The road to the King's palace is not always easy, Christian. There will be hard days. Be brave, keep going, and never turn back.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Then I'll be like that knight. I'd rather take a few bruises at that door than turn away from it.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: Next, the Interpreter led him into a dark room. In the corner sat a man inside an iron cage, with his head hanging low.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Friend... who are you? How did you come to be here?

beats.speaker: Caged Man
beats.text: I was once a follower of the King, and I was glad. But I stopped watching over my heart. One wrong choice... then another... then another.

beats.speaker: Caged Man
beats.text: Now my heart has grown so hard, I can't find my way back. I'm shut in a cage I built for myself.

beats.speaker: Interpreter
beats.text: Remember this man, Christian. Never play with sin, not even a little. Keep your heart soft, and when you go wrong, run straight back to the King.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: God help me to watch over my heart, and keep it soft, every single day.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: In the last room, a man sat up in his bed. He was shaking all over, and his brow was wet with fear.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Why are you trembling so?

beats.speaker: Dreamer
beats.text: I had a dream! The sky went dark as night. A trumpet sounded, and I saw the King on a great white throne.

beats.speaker: Dreamer
beats.text: Everyone had to stand before Him... and I was not ready!

beats.speaker: Interpreter
beats.text: One day that dream will come true, for everyone. So live each day ready to meet the King, Christian, and that day will be a day of joy, not fear.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: I'll remember this room longest of all. It makes me a little afraid... and very glad I'm on the King's road.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: At last, they came to the door at the end of the house.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Thank you, sir, with all my heart. The dust and the water, the fire and the oil, the knight, the cage, and the dream. I'll carry every one of them with me.

beats.speaker: Interpreter
beats.text: Go then, Christian, and the Lord be with you on the King's Highway. Let what you've seen here make you brave, and comfort you on the road.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: So Christian set off again, still carrying his heavy burden. But just ahead, on a little hill, something was waiting that would change everything.
beats.say: So Christian set off again, still carrying his heavy burden. But just ahead, on a little hill, something was waiting... that would change everything.
